**Figure 4. Large-scale OpenScope recordings provide a within-area benchmark for functional heterogeneity.**

**A)** Locations of 4 V1 recording sites in the MouseV2 OpenScope dataset, displayed on the dorsal Allen CCFv3 atlas. Large outlined circles indicate arithmetic mean anterior–posterior and medial–lateral coordinates across 8 animals; smaller points show individual penetrations. Colors identify anterior, lateral, posterior, medial sampling locations. Positions represent the most superficial electrode assigned to V1 on each probe. All 32 positions contribute to the means, including 2 outside the atlas’s dorsal V1 outline. This is an average layout across animals.

**B)** Schematic of 12 two-photon imaging fields of view in a single mouse, overlaid on a widefield retinotopic map. Colors distinguish imaging locations for visualization and do not indicate anatomical groups.

**C–D)** Session-level time to first spike (TTFS), phase modulation (log10 F1/F0), and neuronal response timescale across 4 V1 sampling locations in MouseV2 (**C**) and 5 higher visual areas—LM, RL, AL, PM, AM—in the Allen Brain Observatory Neuropixels dataset (**D**). Points represent session means; shaded half-violins show their distributions, and colored bars and whiskers indicate means and normal-approximation 95% confidence intervals. Locations are treated categorically. MouseV2 analyses include only neurons whose extremum electrode is assigned to V1; session-by-location groups with fewer than 5 eligible neurons are excluded.

**E)** Variation associated with recording location. Colored circles show bias-corrected explained variance (ω²), expressed as a percentage. From top to bottom, rows show: V1 group vs HVA group; Within V1; Across HVAs; Across HVAs vs within V1. The Within V1 and Across HVAs rows quantify location effects; the Across HVAs vs within V1 row shows their difference (HVA minus V1), expressed in percentage points. The positive control (**†**) uses matched Allen sessions, pairing each session’s V1 mean with the equally weighted mean of its available HVA means (45, 28, 53 session pairs for TTFS, F1/F0, and timescale, respectively). Its variance denominator differs from those of the location comparisons.

Colored whiskers indicate 95% percentile intervals from 5,000 whole-session bootstrap replicates. Open gray squares and gray whiskers indicate the median and central 95% range of 5,000 within-session label shuffles. The control shuffles V1/HVA labels within pairs; location comparisons shuffle available location labels within each session. Single-location sessions cannot change under this shuffle. The effect-difference row shows the difference between independently shuffled HVA and V1 estimates.

For the V1 group vs HVA group, Within V1, and Across HVAs rows, significance labels denote uncorrected, one-sided shuffle tests: \* *p* < .05, \*\* *p* < .01, \*\*\* *p* < .001; n.s., *p* ≥ .05. For the effect-difference row, n.s. (**‡**), when present, indicates that the bootstrap interval includes zero; this is not a shuffle-test result. All three difference intervals include zero, leaving the relative magnitudes unresolved. Negative explained-variance estimates are retained as a consequence of bias correction.

**F–G)** Single-neuron response-timescale distributions across V1 locations (**F**) and HVAs (**G**). Kernel-density distributions give equal weight to each session and to each neuron within a session; repeated estimates from a neuron share its weight. Vertical lines indicate weighted medians, and annotations report unique-neuron and session counts. The displayed range is 0–150 ms. MouseV2 neurons satisfy the same anatomical V1 restriction used in C–E.
